item.title: ‘Kaantha’ (2025): A Film About Filmmaking That Doesn’t Quite Deliver
item.description: 'Kaantha' gives us an inside look into the unforgiving world of the film industry and its implications on filmstars who are driven to the edge of self-destruction. The post ‘Kaantha’ (2025): A Film About Filmmaking That Doesn’t Quite Deliver appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: When Women And Queer Artists Had To Become Men To Be Seen
item.description: Women’s expression was coded as too emotional, domestic, or secondary. Queer expression was sanitized or erased. The post When Women And Queer Artists Had To Become Men To Be Seen appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Bhuri Bai: Mural Meets Memoir And More
item.description: Bhuri Bai’s mural is her memoir. While the entire mural looks like a single painting, which it is, it can be actually read in thirty-six parts that chronicles her journey. The post Bhuri Bai: Mural Meets Memoir And More appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Luck Is Just A Grope Away: The Fetishisation Of The Bronze Body And The Haptic Violation Of Gendered Art
item.description: If we want a world where living bodies are safe, we must start by examining why we think "luck" is something that can be squeezed out of a non-consenting bronze breast. The post Luck Is Just A Grope Away: The Fetishisation Of The Bronze Body And The Haptic Violation Of Gendered Art appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Gender Confrontations: An Analysis Of Self-Portraits By Women Artists In India
item.description: The journey of self-portraiture by women artists in India is a journey from silence to scream. The post Gender Confrontations: An Analysis Of Self-Portraits By Women Artists In India appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: The Ephemerality Of A Rangoli And Art That Refuses To Be Owned
item.description: A rangoli expects that you look down carefully and not crush someone’s labour and faith. It trains the body into tiny acts of respect. That is a different, quieter kind of power, but no less real. The post The Ephemerality Of A Rangoli And Art That Refuses To Be Owned appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: The Privileged Feminism Of ‘People We Meet On Vacation’: A Review
item.description: 'People We Meet on Vacation' is ultimately a charming fantasy of "leisure feminism" that mistakes privilege for universal empowerment. The post The Privileged Feminism Of ‘People We Meet On Vacation’: A Review appeared first on Feminism in India.
